general.q: Which city is the federal seat and de facto capital of Switzerland?
general.why: Bern has been the seat of the Swiss federal government since 1848, though Zurich is larger.

general.q: Which spice is produced from the lacy outer covering of the nutmeg seed?
general.why: Mace is made from the dried, reddish outer skin (aril) that wraps around the nutmeg seed.

general.q: In which 1415 battle did English forces under King Henry V defeat a French army?
general.why: Henry V's famous victory at Agincourt took place on St Crispin's Day, 25 October 1415.

general.q: Which English word originally meant 'ignorant' or 'foolish' in Middle English?
general.why: Nice derived from the Latin 'nescius' (ignorant) and gradually shifted in meaning over time.

general.q: What is the anatomical name for the human shoulder blade?
general.why: The scapula connects the upper arm bone with the collarbone at the back of the shoulder.

pop.q: In the sitcom The Inbetweeners, what model of car does Simon's dad buy him, complete with a yellow door?
pop.why: Simon's red Fiat Cinquecento (Hawaii Edition) famously lost its passenger door during a trip to Thorpe Park.

pop.q: In the 1997 Nintendo 64 game GoldenEye 007, which character was banned in multiplayer for being too short?
pop.why: Oddjob's short height made him much harder to hit, leading to a widespread multiplayer etiquette ban.

pop.q: Which Scottish soft drink was famously advertised with the tagline 'Made in Scotland from girders'?
pop.why: Irn-Bru used the famous 'girders' slogan for decades to highlight its bold flavour and rust-like colour.

pop.q: Which iconic 1980s puzzle toy was invented by Hungarian architecture professor Ernő Rubik?
pop.why: Ernő Rubik invented the 3x3 Magic Cube in 1974 to help his students understand three-dimensional geometry.

pop.q: In the 2007 comedy film Hot Fuzz, what is the name of the seemingly idyllic village PC Nicholas Angel is sent to?
pop.why: Sandford is the fictional village home to the Neighbourhood Watch Alliance in Edgar Wright's comedy.

music.q: Which novelty act beat Westlife to secure the UK Christmas Number 1 single in 2000?
music.why: Neil Morrissey voiced Bob the Builder, whose cover of 'Can We Fix It?' topped the festive chart in 2000.

music.q: What was the title of Pulp's critically acclaimed 1995 album featuring 'Common People' and 'Disco 2000'?
music.why: 'Different Class' won the 1996 Mercury Prize and reached number one on the UK Albums Chart.

music.q: Which Leeds rock band released their smash hit debut album 'Employment' in 2005?
music.why: 'Employment' included hit singles 'I Predict a Riot' and 'Oh My God', selling over two million copies.

music.q: Which synth-pop group had the UK Christmas Number 1 in 1981 with 'Don't You Want Me'?
music.why: 'Don't You Want Me' was the biggest-selling single of 1981 in the UK.

music.q: Which pop star spent 10 consecutive weeks at UK Number 1 in 2007 with the single 'Umbrella'?
music.why: Rihanna's hit featured Jay-Z and became the longest-running UK number one single of the 2000s.

mix.q: Which English rock band released the hit album 'Urban Hymns' in 1997?
mix.why: Urban Hymns was one of the biggest-selling albums of the 90s, powered by 'Bitter Sweet Symphony'.

mix.q: What is the largest national park in Great Britain by land area?
mix.why: The Cairngorms National Park in Scotland covers over 4,500 square kilometres.

mix.q: In the classic sitcom Father Ted, on which fictional Irish island is the parish set?
mix.why: Ted and Dougal live in the parochial house on the bleak Craggy Island.

mix.q: Which gas makes up approximately 78% of the Earth's atmosphere?
mix.why: Nitrogen is by far the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere.

mix.q: Which pop group released the hit single 'Karma Chameleon' in 1983?
mix.why: Fronted by Boy George, Culture Club topped the charts worldwide with Karma Chameleon.

mix.q: In the 1996 film Trainspotting, which actor played the unhinged character Francis Begbie?
mix.why: Robert Carlyle gave a terrifyingly memorable performance as the violent Begbie.

mix.q: Who was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom when World War II broke out in 1939?
mix.why: Neville Chamberlain declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.

mix.q: Which indie band released the critically acclaimed debut album 'Silent Alarm' in 2005?
mix.why: Silent Alarm was a landmark UK indie post-punk revival album of the mid-2000s.

mix.q: Which blue video game character made his debut on the Sega Mega Drive in 1991?
mix.why: Sonic became Sega's iconic mascot created to compete with Nintendo's Mario.

mix.q: What type of spirit forms the traditional base of a Mojito cocktail?
mix.why: A traditional Cuban Mojito combines white rum, sugar, lime, soda water, and mint.
